1.explanation: The heart of the bug is the constant NUMBER in src/languages/elixir.js. Its regex only matches nonzero‐leading decimal integers (1–9…), hex/octal/binary forms, and floats whose integer part starts 1–9. It omits \b0\b and decimal/float literals beginning with 0 (e.g. 0, 0123, 0.3). To fix the highlighting, the NUMBER pattern must be extended to include standalone zero and zero‐prefixed decimal/floats.
1.bug_scenario: In the Elixir syntax highlighter (hljs 10.7.1), the numeric‐literal regex doesn’t match a literal “0” or any decimal integers/floats that begin with 0. As a result, “0” by itself, “0123” and the leading “0” in floats like “0.3” are not classified as numbers (only “3” is). The attached screenshot shows every line as a valid number but the “0” values remain unhighlighted.

2.explanation: In src/languages/elixir.js the NUMBER constant defines the regex used to identify numeric literals. Its pattern for decimal numbers is “(-?\b[1-9][0-9_]*(\.[0-9_]+([eE][-+]?[0-9]+)?)?)”, which only matches numbers whose integer part begins with 1–9. As a result, “0”, any integer with a leading zero, and floats with a leading zero (e.g. 0.3) are never matched. To fix the highlighting of zero and zero-prefixed numbers, the regex must be updated to allow an initial “0” (and “0.” for floats) in addition to the existing 1–9 pattern.
2.bug_scenario: The screenshot shows that numeric literals in Elixir code are not being highlighted correctly: the literal “0” on its own isn’t highlighted, decimal numbers starting with zero (e.g. “0123”) aren’t highlighted at all, and floats beginning with “0.” only highlight the part after the decimal point (e.g. in “0.3” only “3” is colored). All of these are valid Elixir numbers and should be marked with the “number” class.
